mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a relative strength in housing, which historically precedes a mild equity correction over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which historically precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by at least 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months, combined with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1%, signals a broad-based supply shock that elevates input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 98 for three consecutive months AND RSAFS monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recessionary regime signals an aggressive easing cycle that boosts risk asset valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a synchronized expansion in demand components, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) in more than 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 jobs for four consecutive months signals a significant labor market deterioration, which precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < -100000 for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 105 for three consecutive months, with no corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE < 4%), signals a supply-side expansion without labor market slack, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 105 for three consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in more than 60% of triggered episodes.
